text: Benedikt Auer opened Saltmarsh & Rye on Tuesday evening, filling the narrow Dock Lane storefront with the smell of charred fennel and rye bread. I saw Auer greeting the first customers at the door, sleeves rolled up, before heading back into the open kitchen to plate mussel chowder and pork with apple relish. He told me he had spent “nearly two years” preparing the menu, which draws on coastal recipes from his childhood. By 8.30 p.m., the 42-seat dining room was full, and a waiting line had formed outside despite the drizzle. Manager Selina Pritchard said bookings were already set through next week.
